overview: White ignores the Scandinavian pawn on d5 and plays 2.b4, offering a pawn for rapid development with Bb2 and queenside space. After 2...dxe4 White will aim for Bb2 and quick piece play, but Black can simply keep the extra pawn.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Bb2 and Nc3 and attack the extra pawn
Use the queenside advance for space

black_ideas.idea: Return the pawn at a convenient moment

typical_structures.structure: White queenside pawn advanced on b4

character.notes: Sharp, unusual play with White a pawn down.

gambit.notes: White gives the e4 pawn and can fall behind if Black plays carefully.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly ever play it.

level.notes: Not a good first choice because dubious.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2...e5
sublines_that_differ.how: Black can also decline and hold the centre.

character.reason: White plays for quick development a pawn down and Black must find the right replies.

gambit.reason: White offers the e4 pawn for development and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: 2.b4 is considered unsound against accurate play.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom play 2.b4 here, and it is chosen for surprise.

level.reason: A dubious line is never Beginner, and it needs little theory.

plans.reason: White hopes for a lead in development with Bb2.
